Method of Attack: Spam emails with malicious Word document attachments that download and install malware payloads
Use of PowerShell commands to install payloads after enabling macros
Delivery of secondary malware such as info stealer Trojans and ransomware
Harvesting user credentials, browser history, and sensitive documents
Use of stolen emails from compromised accounts as templates
Exploitation of trending events (e.g., coronavirus) for social engineering
Impacted Systems: Email recipients targeted by spam campaigns
Attack Vector: Phishing emails using stolen email templates
Indicators of Compromise: Emails with Japanese subject lines and filenames containing the word 'notification' in Japanese
Emails warning of coronavirus infections in Japanese prefectures (e.g., Osaka, Gifu, Tottori)
Attachments prompting users to 'Enable Content' to activate macros
Spam emails camouflaged as official notifications from disability welfare service providers and public health centers
